questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Colombia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Colombia article.

questions.proof: The capital of Colombia is Bogotá.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Colombia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Colombia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Colombia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Colombia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Colombia article.

questions.proof: The countries that have borders on the continent with Colombia are: Venezuela (east), Brazil (southeast), Peru (south), Ecuador (southwest) and Panama (west).

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bogotá?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Colombia is Bogotá.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Colombia about 1,141,748 square kilometres; Guyana about 214,970 square kilometres; El Salvador about 21,041 square kilometres; The Bahamas about 13,878 square kilometres.
